summary.headline: Centum Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 11% YoY to INR205 crore; order book ~INR1,800 crore (+31% YoY), with overseas exit adding a INR94 crore one-time gain.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 11% YoY to INR205 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.28% and PAT margin of 6.59%, which management said was held back by lower BTS contribution and project phasing. Consolidated revenue was INR204 crore (+14% YoY), and consolidated PAT of INR106 crore includes a one-time INR94 crore deconsolidation gain from the overseas subsidiaries; profit from continuing operations was INR11 crore. Standalone order inflow was about INR360 crore (+70% YoY), with BTS inflow of INR120 crore (+150% YoY). Management asked investors to judge the year on a full-year basis, citing stronger execution expected in later quarters.

segments.name: BTS (build-to-spec, defence and space)
segments.commentary: Order book grew ~40% YoY and order inflow was INR120 crore (+150% YoY), but quarterly revenue was held back by project execution schedules. About two-thirds of the ~INR210 crore advances are from BTS.

segments.name: EMS (electronic manufacturing services)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% YoY and order book rose 23% YoY. EMS EBITDA is benchmarked at about 10-11% on a cost-plus model.

segments.name: Semiconductor equipment (within EMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue was practically zero in FY25, exceeded INR100 crore in FY26, and management targets USD25-30 million in the next 1-2 years, with a global OEM as customer.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth of about 25% for FY27 and sees similar visibility for FY28.
EBITDA margin aim is above 13% for FY27 (FY26 reported about 12.5%), with stability or slight improvement expected in FY28; FY28 commentary is preliminary.
Export share of revenue expected at about 50-55% or slightly higher.
BTS to EMS revenue mix expected at roughly 70:30, possibly marginally tilted toward BTS over 1-2 years.
Standalone capex at KIADB Aerospace Park: about INR50-70 crore estimate, with spend largely starting toward the end of FY28; no Centum capex this year because the land is held by a group company.
Export BTS margin target is around 20-plus percent.
Management expects a strong SBS (space-based surveillance) order intake this year.
capex_capacity: KIADB Aerospace Park (Bengaluru): design complete, construction to start soon on land owned by a group company; Centum outlay is nil this year, with capex flow expected toward the end of next fiscal.
Full factory, MEP/HVAC, clean room and plant machinery ordering to follow after shell completion.
Engineering team ramp-up in BTS for system integration, with new talent being hired.
NPI process initiated for electrification and grid automation products, expected to contribute meaningfully in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: BTS demand is strong in space, radar, electronic warfare and air navigation; management expects continued strong order intake through the year.

EMS semiconductor equipment: products in serial production after full qualification; new part numbers are being added. Customer IP sits with the customer, which limits selling the same product to rivals.
Competition in EMS is mainly in Southeast Asia (Malaysia); management says it is the main EMS supplier in India for this customer.
A new INR55-odd crore export order was won for complex test systems in aerospace and defence; management says test-system revenue is lumpy and not recurring.
Management says it is in early preliminary talks with other semiconductor customers for India sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: Will BTS revenue recognition accelerate given the order book has nearly doubled since FY24 and project cycles exceed 2.5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects clear strong BTS revenue growth this year and in coming years, with quarterly variation because of lumpy contracts. About two-thirds of the ~INR210 crore advances are from BTS.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor equipment: who are the customers, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: A key global OEM is the customer, ramped over the last year. Revenue was over INR100 crore in FY26 against about zero in FY25, and the target is USD25-30 million in 1-2 years. EBITDA is about 10-11% on cost-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Will BTS revenue mix move sustainably beyond 70:30 in favour of BTS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BTS may be marginally higher over 1-2 years, but not hugely different from the 70:30 split.

qa_highlights.question: Will India revenue growth stay at the medium-term target of 25%-plus this year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company is confident of reaching about 25% and will maintain that target for now.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27/FY28 guidance for revenue, margins and export mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth about 25% for FY27 with similar visibility for FY28. Margin aim is above 13% in FY27. Export share is about 50-55% or higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the KIADB Aerospace Park facility and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Design is complete and construction is starting soon on group-owned land, so no Centum capex this year. Capex of INR50-70 crore could start toward the end of next fiscal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the export BTS opportunity and its margin?
qa_highlights.answer: An export electronic-warfare BTS opportunity is at an early stage. Margin target is around 20-plus percent, and export system-level deals may carry higher margins because they are not tender-based.

risks_watch: Q1 was described as muted; the full-year growth and margin targets depend on a sharp pick-up in BTS execution in Q2-Q4.
Margin was 11.28% standalone EBITDA, below the >13% FY27 aim, so H2 execution must lift the mix.
Semiconductor-equipment revenue depends on a single global OEM and on semiconductor capex cycles; management flagged possible variability.
Test-system and certain BTS revenues are lumpy and volatile, per management.
Consolidated PAT of INR106 crore is inflated by INR94 crore one-time gain; continuing-ops PAT was only INR11 crore.
Monitor SBS and EW order conversion, and first deliveries for UHM, Virupaksha and TACAN programmes.
Watch for direct armed-forces system-level orders and first DLM (design-led manufacturing) wins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and the order book, but candid that Q1 was muted on growth and margins. Management was evasive on specific customer names and on FY28 margins, and it said these would be updated as opportunities mature.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated profit from continuing operations after tax
Consolidated PAT incl. one-time deconsolidation gain

key_quotes: At the outset, I would like to highlight that the first quarter was somewhat muted compared with our expectations for the full year, both in terms of growth and margins.
So I would say majority of that is coming from the BTS segment only. About two-thirds is coming from the BTS.
We will reach. We are confident of reaching that 25% level, and we'll maintain that for now.
Also, in the last year itself for all the products that are already in production, we have gone through the full qualification process and requirements.
But I would not say it is hugely different. I mean, we may have, instead of 70-30 split, it may marginally be favorable towards the BTS side.
